titles: Promoting Green Growth and low carbon economic transition in South East Asia
descriptions: The project is designed to encourage the adoption of low carbon growth policy and low carbon business in South East Asia by establishing a platform for policy makers and the private sector to engage.

titles: Development Costs of ODA Projects in Asia Pacific Region
descriptions: Project facilitation costs covering planning, implementation and resources as part of ODA projects in Asia Pacific Region.

titles: Administrative Costs of ODA Projects in Asia Pacific Region
descriptions: Project facilitation costs covering planning, implementation, monitoring and resources as part of ODA projects in the Asia Pacific Region.

titles: Administrative and Monitoring Costs for Scoping Studies in Asia Pacific Region
descriptions: The scoping studies aim to provide analysis of various thematic areas to help identify where the current constraints, challenges and opportunities lie, in view of better targeted future programme activity.

titles: Administrative Costs of ODA Projects in Asia Pacific Region
descriptions: Project facilitation costs covering planning, implementation and resources as part of ODA projects in the Asia Pacific Region.

titles: Argentina: promote the adoption of open data practices to improve competitiveness in public procurement tenders at the Buenos Aires city government
descriptions: To increase transparency, competitiveness and efficiency in the Buenos Aires City Government Procurement Process, increasing opportunities for businesses, by supporting the opening up of the data of the on-line system through which Buenos Aires purchases goods and services.

titles: Supporting regulatory reform in South East Asia to improve the business environment in the region and assist economic development
descriptions: The project is designed to build capacity and provide expert UK government resource to assist in the development and delivery of regulatory reform initiatives to the South East Asia region. This will develop trade and investment opportunities for business, increase the transparency of regulatory environments and therefore create business environments in which international and domestic businesses can have confidence to trade, invest and grow.

titles: Improving transparency and accountability in public infrastructure investment in South East Asia
descriptions: The project is designed to provide a comprehensive understanding of the Construction Sector Transparency Initiative (CoST), as an international accountability standard and practical tool that works to improve the business environment, increases competitiveness; levels the playing field, promotes regulatory and policy reforms; and mitigates corruption within public infrastructure investments in Indonesia, Malaysia, Burma, Philippines, Thailand and Vietnam.

titles: Supporting development of infrastructure programmes in SE Asia so they meet international standards and enable confidence of international investors
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to transform the planning, preparation, evaluation and project initiation of South East Asian infrastructure programmes in accordance with world-class methodologies based on UK best practice. This will ensure that projects can be successfully brought to market, and provide bidding and advisory opportunities for international financiers and infrastructure players, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting increased transparency and higher standards in infrastructure projects in South East Asia
descriptions: The project is designed to support ASEAN governments in South East Asia by ensuring their effective use of highly skilled international transaction advisors in the project preparation phase, thereby enhancing the potential of the Public-Private Partnership/infrastructure pipeline. This will encourage increased international investment.

titles: Supporting the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) to strengthen private sector commitment to tackle corruption in South East Asia
descriptions: The project is designed to enable ASEAN to support private sector groups and relevant stakeholders to tackle corruption effectively by promoting regional cooperation, joint advocacy, capacity building, and harmonisation of standards. This is expected to lead to ASEAN's implementation of a regional cooperation model, which will help create a level playing field for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the improvement of the Intellectual Property policy framework in the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN).
descriptions: The project is designed to increase the respect and protection of intellectual property (IP) in South East Asia. Bringing IP policies to the same standard across the region, and more in line with international and global standards. This is expected to lead to the development of ASEAN-wide policies on trademark protection and other IP issues; as well as support innovation and productivity growth in the region. It is also expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Producing a Scoping Study for a South East Asia Future Cities Programme
descriptions: The project is designed to scope the opportunities for a future Prosperity Fund (PF) programme on Future Cities in South East Asia (SEA) and inform the development of the concept note and business case for a PF programme on Future Cities in SEA.

titles: Scoping study to analyse health systems for the Better Health programme
descriptions: Scoping study to develop a programme to improve health systems in targeted ODA-eligible countries.

titles: Improving Trade Facilitation Indicators in Brazil to promote trade reforms and increased prosperity
descriptions: Create a Trade Reform Plan for Brazil using performance indicators to identify trade efficiency gaps, paving the way for trade cost reductions and increase in imports and exports flows.

titles: Creating a coherence model for Trade Regulations in Brazil to support a better business environment
descriptions: Increase Brazilian capacity to facilitate investment and increase international trade flows by improving domestic regulatory measures (regulatory coherence), using UK as a model.

titles: Improving the quality of public spending in Brazil through structured policy evaluation methodologies
descriptions: The project will contribute to improved quality of public spending in Brazil by increasing its ability to evaluate the impact of fiscal policies and government spending policies on the private sector.

titles: Increasing efficiency and performance of the Brazilian judiciary system in Brazil to support the fight against corruption
descriptions: The project will increase efficiency in judiciary system management and foster better justice services in Brazil to combat organised crime, corruption and money laundering.

titles: Supporting a new Open Innovation policy in Health for the State of Sao Paulo
descriptions: This project will help deliver a more efficient public health system in São Paulo state through an open innovation approach, fostering entrepreneurship and developing public-private partnerships.

titles: Teacher Training for Technical and Vocational Education in Brazil
descriptions: This project will help strengthen delivery of vocational and technical education in Brazil's Federal Institutes in order to deploy a more skilled workforce to address the needs of industry, making Brazil more attractive for international companies.

titles: Energy Storage in Brazil: promoting low-carbon technology development through innovative regulation and public policies
descriptions: The project will support development of low-carbon energy security in Brazil by equipping its electricity sector with storage technologies.

titles: Oil & Gas: increasing productivity and improving oil spills detection to promote sustainable sector growth in Brazil
descriptions: This project will improve oil and gas sector efficiency, sustainability and transparency by maximizing operational efficiency for monitoring oil and gas spills, increasing compliance and reducing costs for both government and international companies.

titles: Oil and gas decommissioning guidance to develop a strong regulatory framework, guide sustainable sector development and protect the environment
descriptions: By providing guidance on oil and gas decommission to develop a regulatory framework, the project will help update the Brazilian offshore oil & gas regulatory framework on operational safety, environmental protection and cost effectiveness, setting clear decommissioning guidance for the industry. This will also make the sector more attractive for international companies.

titles: Health Accelerator Programme: re-balancing primary healthcare policy in Recife
descriptions: This project will support reform of primary care services in the city of Recife, improving access, responsiveness, quality and range of services, to make healthcare in Brazil more cost-effective and also attractive to foreign investment. This is through supporting local commissioners and clinicians by bringing together data collected in the city of Recife to accelerate the development of unplanned / urgent care services so that citizens can have their care provided locally.

titles: Roadmap for Logistics Infrastructure Investments in Brazil: improving regulation to facilitate private sector investments and foster economic growth
descriptions: This project will promote policy reform and private investment in logistics infrastructure by producing a roadmap for Brazil's logistics infrastructure regulatory framework, to facilitate private sector investments and foster economic growth.

titles: Enabling Smart Cities in Brazil: supporting the expansion of intermodal transport with smart technologies to improve urban mobility
descriptions: This project will provide the city of Belo Horizonte with enhanced smart cities capabilities by incorporating low-carbon and innovative UK-based technologies and establishing strategic partnerships with UK cities.

titles: Enhancing Education, Health, and Mobility Infrastructure through Public-Private Partnerships in Brazil
descriptions: The project supports the states of Minas Gerais and Bahia in Brazil in the development of Public Private Partnerships (PPPs) in the education, health and urban mobility sectors, by providing technical assistance before the competitive tendering procedure, resulting in a more favorable business environment for PPPs, with more transparency and efficiency, improved regulation and commercial integration.

titles: Brazil Low Carbon Infrastructure Plan: developing a Green Bonds market in Brazil to leverage private finance for low carbon infrastructure
descriptions: This project will support development of low-carbon and climate resilient infrastructure in Brazil by developing a Green Bonds market in Brazil to leverage private finance for low carbon infrastructure

titles: Brazil: Sustainable Wastewater Management in Minas Gerais: providing international best practices on wastewater management to promote sustainability
descriptions: This project will support Minas Gerais state government in the reform of its sewage system and implement new sustainable sanitation infrastructure, providing international best practices on wastewater management to promote sustainability, reducing environmental impacts and improving living conditions.

titles: Brazil: Scoping funds to support future development and welfare opportunities in Brazil
descriptions: The scoping study will provide economic analysis of the priority areas of development and welfare in Brazil. This will help identify the immediate and longer-term requirements for Brazil helping to direct future policy and programme activity.

titles: Enhancing urban planning capability in Burma
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to build an urban planning capability within the Burmese Ministry of Construction to provide a framework for sustainable urban development and hence to enable economic growth. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Establishing an Aberdeen-Burma Energy Economy partnership
descriptions: The project will help the Burmese government and industry to learn from Aberdeen's success in developing into a world class sub-sea centre of excellence through knowledge exchange, training and capacity building initiatives. It will help Burma to develop its own Oil and Gas infrastructure and to enhance the capacity of its business community such that it can play an increasing role within Burma and in South East Asia.

titles: Encouraging the liberalisation of the insurance sector in Burma
descriptions: The project is designed to encourage the liberalisation of the insurance sector in Burma with the goal of stimulating economic growth through the creation of a competitive insurance market, subsequently driving social development and promoting cross-border trade through the protection of investors' assets and risks.

titles: Helping Burma implement an Anti-Money Laundering strategy to improve regulation and strengthen robustness in the financial sector
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to support Burma's Central Control Board on Money Laundering by providing technical assistance and strategic support in the country's development of a National Anti-Money Laundering Strategic Plan to achieve rapid progress and reform that supports strong and stable economic growth and tackles important barriers to economic development and international market entry.

titles: Assisting Burma to implement the Paris Agreement on climate change by turning its Intended Nationally Determined Contribution commitment into action
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to develop transparent, measurable and action-orientated implementation plans to deliver the targets and activities identified in the Nationally Determined Contributions of Burma. This will increase private sector involvement, in particular in the low carbon energy sector, by identifying specific investment opportunities for investors and technology providers.

titles: Administrative Costs of ODA Projects in China
descriptions: Project facilitation costs covering planning, implementation and resources as part of ODA projects in China.

titles: Promoting development of green principles in Chinese healthcare, including in infrastructure and service delivery to support sustainable healthcare
descriptions: The project is designed to allow the Chinese government to draw upon UK experience to promote the development of green health and care systems which support intelligent, resilient and sustainable healthcare. It will achieve this by running provincial level pilot initiatives to strengthen the function of health management and promote green infrastructure, operation and service delivery. A final workshop will present to Chinese Ministries an overview of international case studies on sustainable healthcare, including from the UK, and will generate options for China's adoption of green principles in its healthcare systems.

titles: Supporting China to increase capacity in international tax cooperation
descriptions: The project is designed to enable Her Majesty's Revenue and Customs and China's State Administration of Taxation to work together through the Forum on Tax Administration (FTA), holding bilateral and multilateral Tax Administration discussions to drive forward G20 tax priorities and support China's joint role as G20 president and host of the FTA Plenary.

titles: Supporting China's Research and Development capabilities through establishing an Innovation Gateway in Shanghai
descriptions: The project is designed to build a platform that assists the local government and Research and Development base in Shanghai to facilitate academia-industry collaboration. By doing this, the project intends to make China's Research and Development more competitive internationally, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Establishing a platform for safety testing of cosmetics in China to eliminate unnecessary animal testing and align with international norms
descriptions: This project is designed to draw on UK expertise to establish a platform for the safe testing of cosmetics in China, which eliminates unnecessary animal testing. It is intended that, by 2018, China's cosmetic regulators will be engaged in economic and trade policy coordination with the UK and will begin reform of China's regulations, toward alternative approaches to ones involving animal testing. This is expected to lead to an improvement in the sustainability of industry growth, and facilitate the removal of trade barriers, thus generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting Chinese efforts to re-use brownfield and marginal land for low carbon and renewable energy purposes
descriptions: The project is designed to promote China-UK collaboration to evaluate and adapt innovative methodologies, in order that China can re-use brownfields and marginal land for low carbon and renewable energy purposes. This is intended to support the development of low-resource strategies for land management, decontamination of land, urban regeneration, and community enterprise for brownfield and marginal land areas. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Designing a power market protocol for China that enables better renewable energy integration
descriptions: The project is designed to support China's orientation towards renewable energy by producing proposals for adoption by China's National Energy Administration. These include proposals, based on UK and US experience, for a market model, pricing mechanism and operation rules. The proposals will serve as a source of reference for China for its creation of a more competitive power market.

titles: Strengthening China's evidence discovery procedure in intellectual property litigation
descriptions: The project is designed to draw upon UK and EU experience to develop China's trademark system and brand management practice by working with its government and its legal and industrial sectors raising awareness and capacity building. This is intended to enhance the institutional environment for brand operations of companies operating in China, including UK ones. For example, they will be better-placed to protect their revenues and derive further income by licensing or sale of brand rights.

titles: Supporting the national rollout of provincial level climate legislation in China
descriptions: The project is designed to refine draft climate legislation in China by drawing on international best practice and feeding in key findings from four provinces that already have climate regulation - Jiangsu, Hubei, Shijiazhuang and Nanchang. The project will involve seminars in these four provinces to share practices and experience, plus the submission to the Chinese government of a final report that advises on national and provincial policy.

titles: Supporting the adoption of a roadmap in Sichuan province on the development of alternative energy sources in China
descriptions: The project is designed to support Sichuan's adoption of a roadmap to support its development of alternative energy sources. The implementer will produce recommendations to Sichuan's government on improving regulations for shale gas development. It is intended that this leads to Sichuan's adoption of the recommendations, leading to a national pilot project in 2-3 years time.

titles: Promoting UK-China collaborations in areas such as co-productions and film exports, to support economic reform and diversification in China.
descriptions: The project is designed to support the internationalisation of the Chinese film industry by enhancing UK-China collaborations particularly in areas such as co-productions and film exports. This will include improving policy skills, expertise and policy frameworks that support China's engagement in international markets. It is intended that UK and Chinese industries develop a relationship that fosters an increased understanding of each others' creative and commercial working practices. This will help facilitate co-productions more effectively and increase the competitiveness of Chinese films internationally, thereby promoting economic rebalancing in China and generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting policy in China by holding the Second UK-China Forum on Social Policy and Public Sector Reform
descriptions: The project is designed to bring together influential officials, scholars and practitioners from China and the UK at a Second UK-China Forum on Social Policy and Public Sector Reform, in order to influence central government policy, social policy issues and public sector reform in line with China's 13th Five-Year Plan. The targeted policy areas include open data, civil contingency, public service delivery and government performance evaluation.

titles: Supporting China's ability to monitor greenhouse gas emissions
descriptions: The project is designed to improve China's monitoring of its greenhouse gas emissions, to encourage China's move to low carbon production, thereby decreasing the risk from Climate Change. This will be achieved by establishment of a set of indicators that will regularly provide government leaders with a clear assessment of the risk of following a high emissions pathway, and the priority actions needed to avoid it.

titles: Supporting China's ability to monitor climate risks.
descriptions: The project is designed to improve China's monitoring of climate risks, helping to develop China's markets in climate resilient infrastructure and insurance. This will be achieved by establishing a set of climate risk indicators that will regularly provide government leaders with a clearer assessment of risk than is currently available, thereby generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting public engagement and consultation on China's design and delivery of energy projects
descriptions: The project is designed to share UK and international experience in developing more effective public engagement and consultation, in order to improve the planning and implementation of both China and UK energy projects. This will include sharing experience to improve government, regulators' and companies' ability to understand and address public hopes and concerns with regard to the delivery of energy infrastructure plans in China and the UK, through effective communication and engagement.

titles: Supporting China's transition to low carbon energy by enhancing its government's capability to monitor energy statistics
descriptions: The project is designed to increase knowledge and use – at both national and provincial government level in China - of best practice methodologies, and internationally-agreed concepts and definitions in energy statistics. It is intended that China's energy statistics capability is thereby enhanced, enabling China to monitor energy policy through its transition to low carbon. Doing so will align China's data collection with OECD countries, which will accelerate China's transition to low carbon growth.

titles: Strengthening primary care capacity in China through training to help the health of the poor while creating openings for international and UK business
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to strengthen the training of Chinese GPs in paediatrics to improve their skills across diagnoses and treatments, in pilot cities. This project will enable primary care institutions to take on more responsibilities in dealing with child medical issues, relieving pressure on tertiary paediatric services. Chinese policy makers will use the pilot report to inform the establishment of tiered treatment guidelines. This is expected to generate commercial and collaborative opportunities for international entities, including UK ones.

titles: Improving the efficiency of electricity markets in Yunnan, China
descriptions: The project is designed to improve the efficiency of electricity markets in China, through a pilot project on reforming electricity wholesale and retail markets in Yunnan Province. In doing this, it will draw upon UK policy and market expertise to inform and accelerate Yunnan's power market pilot, facilitating the transition to low carbon of the world's largest power sector. This will generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Reducing greenhouse gas emissions in China by storage of carbon dioxide in depleted gas reservoirs.
descriptions: The project is designed to use UK expertise to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by developing the storage of carbon dioxide in depleted gas reservoirs. It is intended that China's Ministry of Science and Technology adopts policy recommendations on such storage, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Sustaining the rapid growth of China's Green Bond Market
descriptions: The project is designed to draw upon the UK's leadership in global financial markets to sustain the rapid growth of China's Green Bond Market, which involves proceeds of bonds being allocated to environmental projects, and contributes to reduction of emissions. It is intended to enhance the connection between China's domestic green bond market and the international market. It is also intended to establish green bonds as a tool for China to tap into international capital markets to finance low-carbon and climate resilient projects, which would open up opportunities for international business, including UK companies.

titles: Improving China's protection of intellectual property rights, including its copyright collective licensing system.
descriptions: The project is designed to improve China's copyright collective licensing system and improve UK-China cooperation on dispute resolution. It is intended that, by January 2018, better resolution of disputes results in Chinese judges' increased awareness and consequent policy input to ongoing copyright reforms, thereby leading to higher revenues for Chinese and international creative industries companies (including UK ones) and individual creators.

titles: Supporting the improvement of Chinese labour standards
descriptions: This is a project designed to support the improvement of Chinese labour standards in the restructuring of the country's manufacturing sector, in line with the relevant UN guiding principles. In doing so, it intends to promote fundamental workers' rights in China's rapidly-changing manufacturing sector, by equipping companies to change their business and human rights policy in order to address high-risk issues that obstruct implementation of the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights. This is intended to benefit the Chinese workforce and the supply chain management of Chinese and international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the strengthening of competition policy in China
descriptions: The project is designed to support China's National Development and Reform Commission to develop and adopt a policy framework and implementation path, in order to establish the mechanism of fair competition scrutiny. This is intended to create a better and fairer business environment in China, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting China's development of its regulatory regime for private equity and hedge funds
descriptions: The project is designed to support the strengthening and refinement of China's hedge fund and private equity fund regulatory framework, in order to build a more robust financial system in China and encourage foreign participation in the Chinese private fund industry. In doing so, it is also expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting China to further develop and open up its commodities derivatives market, through an initial focus in Guangdong province
descriptions: The project is designed to support China to further develop and open up its commodities derivatives market, though an initial focus on Guangdong province. It is intended that, by December 2017, Guangdong government will introduce practical plans aimed at the further opening of commodities futures, especially precious metals and non-ferrous metals, to international markets as part of the wider strategy of internationalising the RMB. This will benefit China and provide better access to Chinese capital markets for international (including UK) investors.

titles: Supporting the development of the Chinese anti-money laundering framework
descriptions: The project is designed to provide technical support to China's anti-money laundering framework in order to support preparation for the Financial Action Task Force Mutual Evaluation. This contributes to ensuring the integrity of China's financial system, helping to provide a level playing for businesses, reduces risks and encourages investment from international firms.

titles: Developing China's crowd-funding regulatory policy, to promote China's internet finance market growth
descriptions: The project is designed to draw upon UK experiences and expertise to support China to improve its crowd-funding regulatory policy, and put in place a UK-China framework for crowd-funding cooperation, based on the practices of Guizhou province. The UK-China collaboration will build expertise and create links with key stakeholders in China's internet finance market, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting regulatory reform of the Shenzhen private equity market
descriptions: The project is designed to promote regulatory reform of the Shenzhen private equity market. This supports China's drive to reform its economy under its 13th Five Year Plan, one focus of which is to address the fact that regulation has not kept pace with market development. If enacted, such reform can enable direction of finance in China towards the most innovative and efficient sectors of the economy, to support economic rebalancing, financial inclusion and poverty reduction, particularly for the growth of SMEs. The support is aimed at helping the Shenzhen government introduce a pilot plan with an aim to further broaden and deepen its private equity market through expanding quotas and relaxing regulatory restriction on foreign market participants.

titles: Promoting the development of the market in Chinese local government debt
descriptions: The project takes up an issue discussed in the 2015 UK-China Economic and Financial Dialogue regarding the development of China's local debt markets. It is designed to provide policy suggestions for the development of Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Local Government Debt Issuance in China to be issued by the Ministry of Finance in 2017, thereby generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Applying expertise to science and engineering teaching in China
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to share innovative approaches in the teaching of academic and vocational STEM (Science Technology Education and Mathematics) education, based on successful methodologies developed in the UK, with leading Chinese teachers/schools and Ministries of Education/Science and Technology, thereby benefiting education in China and laying a foundation for long-term collaboration with the UK.

titles: Researching population ageing to support the design of medical reimbursement policies in Shanghai
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to reveal the relationship between age and medical expenses, and the characteristics of end-of-life expenses among the elderly in Shanghai. Through undertaking a ‘value for money' analysis to identify inappropriate resource use on elderly care in Shanghai, and learning lessons from the UK context, this project will provide a reference for policy design and implementation in Shanghai, both under the 13th Five-Year Plan and through guidance that the Shanghai Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau is due to issue on the Elderly Care Social Security System by the end of 2016. Chinese adoption of UK proposals in the study has the potential to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Increasing awareness among Chinese stakeholders about enforcement of intellectual property rights
descriptions: The project is designed to draw upon UK best practice to protect and enforce intellectual property (IP) rights among Chinese rights owners. A UK-China Intellectual Property conference in London will demonstrate UK policy designed to protect IP, which in turn will help support innovation and growth in the respective sectors.

titles: Supporting enterprises in Chongqing, China to manage effective carbon reduction through emissions trading
descriptions: The project is designed to draw upon UK experience and expertise to support Chongqing-based enterprises covered by China's national Emission Trading Scheme, so these enterprises establish their corporate-level carbon management system. In doing so, this is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Developing a human resources strategy for Chongqing's Free Trade Zone
descriptions: The project is designed to draw upon UK experience to support the adoption of a ‘Human Resources Strategy' by the Chongqing government's various human resources departments and Liangjiang New Area's governance structure. It is then intended that these entities will disseminate Chongqing's best practices to other Free Trade Zones in China. This will help open up the market for foreign professional training and qualification service providers, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting Yangtze Delta Region cities with their climate change risk adaption plan
descriptions: The project is designed to develop a climate change self-assessment tool to help Yangtze River Delta Region cities draw up climate change adaptation plans, supporting the efforts of these cities to be among China's National Development and Reform Commission's 30 demonstration cities for climate change adaptation. As the project is implemented, UK expertise on infrastructure policy and services may be accepted by Chinese policy makers, potentially generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the incorporation of climate risk assessment in Shanghai's Water Supply Infrastructure Strategy
descriptions: The project is designed to draw upon UK expertise to influence the Shanghai government's water sector asset investment policy, by providing a robust framework for Climate Change vulnerability assessment. There is potential for such assessment to be replicated to other regions of China. The project will also generate business opportunities for international businesses, including from the UK, to provide equipment, technology and consulting services to the Chinese authorities.

titles: Supporting the internationalisation of China's film industry whilst generating opportunities for international and UK business
descriptions: The project is designed to draw upon the expertise of UK TV professionals so that the Chinese TV sector and relevant Chinese authorities learn a range of new skills, which will enable them to increase their commercial, creative and technical aptitude, enabling them to build capacity. They will build their knowledge and skills to help create an expanding, sustainable and vibrant sector, thereby promoting economic diversification in China and generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Increasing the understanding of stakeholders in Jiangsu, China of the commercial aspects of offshore wind electricity generation
descriptions: The project is intended to increase the understanding of Jiangsu energy regulators and market stakeholders of offshore wind market conditions. This will be achieved through a series of reports that draw upon UK experience. The project will also explain UK policy and commercial solutions in Jiangsu, bolstering sustainable growth of China's largest offshore wind market, accelerating the low carbon transition, enhancing energy security, reducing global technology costs and generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Promoting the development of China's marine energy technology and utilisation
descriptions: The project intends to draw upon UK expertise to promote the development of marine energy technology and utilisation. This will include policy recommendations to China to build a framework for commercialising marine energy technologies and standards. It is hoped that China will adopt the recommendations, establish a Marine Energy Centre, and tap the advantages of marine energy as a new source of renewable energy which can be consistently generated throughout the year. This would also promote creation of a new market and potential opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting independent verification of carbon emissions in Shanghai and neighbouring provinces in China
descriptions: The project is designed to harness UK expertise to support the building of capacity for the independent verification of carbon emissions in Shanghai, as a pilot city for China's National Emissions Trading Scheme. This project will provide a solid model for neighbouring provinces to emulate and support the provision of expertise to create a strong, reliable, business friendly system, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting the development of an Emissions Trading Scheme in South China
descriptions: The project is designed to launch a Carbon Trading platform in south China by June 2017. This project will build on the UK's strong links to Guangdong, collaborate with provinces in the Pan Pearl River Delta, and bring in UK expertise to help all of Southern China build a strong, effective, interconnected carbon trading infrastructure, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting market development and regulatory reform in insurance in Guangdong Nansha Free Trade Zone, China.
descriptions: The project is designed to deliver policy recommendations to the insurance market authorities on relaxing restrictions on foreign insurance companies, focusing on registration of institutions, personnel, and funds in Guangdong Nansha Free Trade Zone. This is expected to generate opportunities for international business, including from the UK.

titles: Assisting the development and application of environmental risk assessment in China's green financial system
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK expertise to further drive the adaptation of natural capital valuation in China's financing and investment decisions by relevant governmental authorities and financial institutions in China's transition to a low carbon and sustainable economy.

titles: Supporting the development of green finance projects in three Chinese cities
descriptions: The project is designed to develop plans or regulations on green finance, assist with the establishment of a green financial system, and introduce green industrial and financial solutions, in three Chinese cities. This is intended to strengthen the development of China's green finance market.

titles: Working with China to improve international cooperation on corruption cases
descriptions: The project is designed to bring together practitioners from leading countries to influence China's G20 Presidency agenda of new solutions for improving international legal assistance in trans-border corruption cases, to be implemented by G20 as well as non-G20 countries. Increased transparency and integrity in trade such as through ensuring customs compliance and better internal controls, will help to improve the business environment which in turn benefits wider society.

titles: Strengthening China's evidence discovery procedure in intellectual property litigation
descriptions: The project is designed to support the protection of intellectual property (IP) rights in China, by the adoption by IP courts in China of policy to develop more effective – but proportionate – evidence discovery procedures in civil court cases, facilitating the determination of infringement of IP rights and calculation of compensatory damages, and benefiting domestic and international (including UK) IP owners.

titles: Supporting China's development of its low-carbon automobile policy to reduce the rapid increase in Chinese vehicle emissions
descriptions: The project is designed to draw on UK collaboration with the Chinese government to study the low-carbon regulations for China's rapidly growing automobile industry and produce a clear roadmap to reducing emissions across the industry. This will result in increasing demand for design and technology, generating opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.

titles: Supporting China's development of a carbon emissions reduction roadmap for the Guangdong transport sector
descriptions: The project is designed to draw upon UK expertise to secure the commitment, by the end of 2017, of Guangdong province to the Carbon Emissions Reduction Roadmap. This will set an ambitious target to reduce emissions in the transportation sector in the 13th Five Year Plan.

titles: Preparing Guangdong's household carbon credit system for national and international adoption
descriptions: The project is designed, through a review of international consumption-based carbon emission reduction reward systems, and the current pilots in Guangdong province, to produce general operating principles for an equivalent system in Guangdong, which can be replicated nationally and internationally. This will be produced for the Guangdong Development and Reform Commission and its pilot cities by March 2017. This is expected to generate opportunities for international businesses, including UK ones.
